mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods following GDPC1 declines, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs increase.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for increased consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% within the last two months signals a strong demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for increased construction and related industries' earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 1% over the last quarter and retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in the last month, it signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% in 1 quarter and RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between GDPC1 and RSAFS increases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
